anchor.note: The anchor is the meaning contrast, not an English suffix. Each language record describes its own number inventory, marking, agreement, and obligatoriness.

scope_note: Learner-facing grammatical number in ordinary noun phrases and agreement. Rules are intentionally language-specific and must not be inherited across languages. A language can be lesson-ready even when its central rule is that nouns normally do not require overt singular/plural marking.

rules.summary_en: Most count nouns contrast singular with plural, and the most common written plural ending is -s or -es.
tips_en: Start with the meaning: one countable thing versus more than one.
Spelling and pronunciation vary, so -s is a pattern rather than the definition of plural.

rules.summary_en: Some common nouns use irregular plurals or no visible singular/plural change.
tips_en: Learn common irregular pairs such as child/children as lexical patterns.
A noun can express plural even when there is no final -s.

rules.summary_en: Number can also affect determiners and present-tense verb agreement.
tips_en: Compare this book / these books.
Look beyond the noun when deciding what number the whole phrase expresses.

rules.summary_en: A noun ending in an unstressed vowel normally forms its plural with -s.
tips_en: libro → libros; casa → casas.
Treat this as the high-frequency first pattern, then learn the smaller ending-specific patterns.

rules.summary_en: Many nouns ending in a consonant form the plural with -es, with spelling or stress adjustments in some words.
tips_en: papel → papeles is a useful model.
Do not mechanically add -es without checking ending-specific spelling rules.

rules.summary_en: Some nouns keep the same surface form in singular and plural, so the surrounding noun phrase carries the contrast.
tips_en: la crisis → las crisis; el lunes → los lunes.
An unchanged noun does not mean the phrase has no grammatical number.

rules.summary_en: Determiners and adjectives normally agree with the noun in number, and subject number can also affect verb agreement.
tips_en: el libro nuevo → los libros nuevos.
la casa blanca → las casas blancas: change the whole agreement chain, not only the noun.

rules.summary_en: French nouns generally contrast singular and plural; written -s is the most common plural marker, with several ending-specific patterns.
tips_en: Do not assume the written plural ending will be pronounced.
Learn frequent ending families and irregular nouns as patterns.

rules.summary_en: Determiners are often the clearest audible and visible cue to noun-phrase number.
tips_en: Watch the article or other determiner as well as the noun.
Number belongs to the noun phrase, not just the final letters of the noun.

rules.summary_en: Adjectives and other agreeing words can also reflect plural number, subject to normal French agreement rules.
tips_en: Track agreement across the phrase.
Written agreement may be clearer than spoken agreement in many forms.

rules.summary_en: Portuguese nouns normally contrast singular and plural; many add -s, while several common endings have their own plural patterns.
tips_en: Start with the noun's ending rather than one universal plural recipe.
Learn frequent irregular or ending-specific plurals with the noun.

rules.summary_en: Articles, determiners, and adjectives normally agree with the noun in number.
tips_en: Change the noun phrase as a unit, not only the noun.
Agreement is often a stronger clue than translating an English plural ending.

rules.summary_en: Subject number normally participates in finite verb agreement.
tips_en: Check whether the subject is singular or plural before choosing a verb form.
Nominal number and verbal person-number agreement are connected but not identical topics.

rules.summary_en: Italian commonly marks plural by changing a noun's final vowel, with major patterns such as -o/-i, -a/-e, and -e/-i plus important exceptions.
tips_en: Think vowel change, not simply add -s.
Gender and noun class help predict the common pattern but do not eliminate exceptions.

rules.summary_en: Some nouns are invariable for number and rely on determiners or context to show singular versus plural.
tips_en: Do not force a visible noun change when the noun class is invariable.
Use the whole noun phrase as evidence.

rules.summary_en: Articles and adjectives normally agree with the noun in number as well as gender.
tips_en: Track article, noun, and adjective together.
A plural noun phrase is an agreement pattern, not only a noun ending.

rules.summary_en: Modern Greek nouns normally distinguish singular and plural, but the actual endings depend on the noun's inflectional class, gender, and case.
tips_en: Learn a noun together with enough of its paradigm to recognize its plural family.
Number cannot be separated completely from case endings in Greek.

rules.summary_en: Articles and adjectives agree with the noun in number as well as other grammatical features.
tips_en: Read the whole noun phrase for number clues.
Agreement can make number visible even before the noun ending is familiar.

rules.summary_en: Subject number is also reflected in ordinary finite verb agreement.
tips_en: Keep noun-phrase agreement and verb agreement conceptually separate, then connect them through the subject.
Do not import English plural endings into Greek morphology.

rules.summary_en: Mandarin common nouns normally do not require a singular-versus-plural inflection.
tips_en: Do not search for a mandatory Chinese equivalent of English -s.
Let context and the rest of the noun phrase establish number when the noun itself is unchanged.

rules.summary_en: Exact quantities are ordinarily expressed with numerals and the appropriate classifier construction.
tips_en: Treat numeral + classifier + noun as a core counting pattern.
The classifier system is not a plural suffix system.

rules.summary_en: The suffix 们 can mark groups with personal pronouns and many human-denoting nouns, but it is not a general plural ending for all nouns.
tips_en: Do not attach 们 mechanically to every noun that is plural in English.
Ask whether the referent and construction naturally license 们.

rules.summary_en: Japanese nouns normally do not inflect obligatorily for singular versus plural.
tips_en: An unchanged noun may refer to one or more than one depending on context.
Do not manufacture a plural marker just because English has one.

rules.summary_en: Counting ordinarily uses numeral and counter constructions rather than plural noun inflection.
tips_en: Learn counters as part of how Japanese packages quantity.
Number marking and counting strategy are related but not the same as an English-style plural ending.

rules.summary_en: Forms such as たち can mark an associated group, especially with people and pronouns, but they are not universal noun plurals.
tips_en: Treat たち as a construction with its own distribution.
Do not attach it to every noun meaning more than one.

rules.summary_en: German has several productive plural patterns rather than one universal plural suffix.
tips_en: Learn a noun together with its plural form.
Common plural signals include -e, -er, -(e)n, -s, zero endings, and sometimes umlaut, but no single cue covers every noun.

rules.summary_en: Number combines with case in the noun phrase, so articles and adjective endings help identify the grammatical form.
tips_en: Read article + adjective + noun as one inflectional package.
Do not confuse plural formation with the separate question of which case the phrase has.

rules.summary_en: Determiners and adjectives reflect number through the German agreement system.
tips_en: Use surrounding agreement as evidence when the noun's plural is unfamiliar.
A plural phrase can be recognizable before you know the noun's exact plural class.

rules.summary_en: Korean nouns normally do not require overt plural marking whenever the meaning is plural.
tips_en: Let context or quantity expressions do the work when they already make number clear.
Do not assume every English plural noun needs a Korean suffix.

rules.summary_en: 들 can make plurality explicit in many contexts, especially with humans or individuated groups, but it is not obligatory for every plural noun.
tips_en: Ask whether plurality needs to be emphasized or disambiguated.
Treat 들 as distribution-sensitive rather than a mechanical English -s equivalent.

rules.summary_en: Numeral and counter constructions are central for explicit quantities.
tips_en: Choose the appropriate counter with the numeral.
Counting syntax can make an additional noun plural marker unnecessary.

rules.summary_en: Standard Arabic productively distinguishes singular, dual, and plural rather than only singular versus plural.
tips_en: Treat exactly two as a grammatical category of its own.
Do not collapse the dual into an ordinary plural when reading or building noun phrases.

rules.summary_en: Arabic plurals include sound patterns and many broken plurals formed by internal stem changes.
tips_en: Learn the plural with nouns whose broken-plural pattern is not predictable enough for you yet.
A plural does not have to be a suffix attached to an unchanged stem.

rules.summary_en: Number interacts with gender, case/state, and agreement, including important special behavior with many non-human plurals.
tips_en: Learn agreement as part of the construction, not as a copy of the noun ending.
Keep the noun's number and the form required on agreeing words as separate questions.

rules.summary_en: Hindi nouns can distinguish singular and plural, with plural behavior depending strongly on gender and the noun's ending/class.
tips_en: Do not expect one plural suffix for every noun.
Learn the noun's gender and inflection pattern together.

rules.summary_en: Number interacts with direct and oblique nominal forms, so a plural can look different before a postposition.
tips_en: Ask both number and syntactic form before choosing the ending.
Do not memorize a plural in isolation from the forms you will meet in sentences.

rules.summary_en: Number can participate in adjective and verb agreement together with gender and other syntactic conditions.
tips_en: Track which element controls the agreement in the sentence.
Number is one feature in a larger agreement system.

rules.summary_en: Ukrainian nouns normally distinguish singular and plural, with endings determined by declension class and case.
tips_en: Learn plural forms together with the declension pattern.
Number and case are expressed in the same inflectional system.

rules.summary_en: Numeral constructions can select forms that do not map neatly onto a simple English singular-versus-plural rule.
tips_en: Learn common numeral + noun patterns as constructions.
Do not decide the noun ending from the numeral's English translation alone.

rules.summary_en: Adjectives and finite verbs can reflect number through agreement.
tips_en: Use agreement cues across the phrase and clause.
Keep case agreement and number agreement connected but conceptually distinct.

rules.summary_en: Russian nouns normally distinguish singular and plural, and the visible ending depends on declension class and case.
tips_en: Learn a noun's plural as part of its declension pattern.
Do not treat a single nominative plural ending as the whole number system.

rules.summary_en: Russian numeral constructions use important form patterns, especially around numerals ending in one, two-to-four, and five or more, subject to the normal compound-numeral rules and exceptions.
tips_en: Learn numeral + noun combinations as constructions rather than translating an English plural mechanically.
Case and the numeral itself both matter.

rules.summary_en: Adjectives and finite verbs can reflect number through agreement.
tips_en: Use surrounding agreement as evidence for the phrase's number.
Remember that past-tense and present/future agreement organize features differently.

rules.summary_en: Turkish marks ordinary nominal plural with -lar or -ler according to vowel harmony.
tips_en: Choose the harmonic variant from the noun's vowels.
The plural marker is regular, but its presence is still construction-dependent.

rules.summary_en: After an exact numeral, the noun normally remains morphologically singular because the quantity is already explicit.
tips_en: iki kitap, not a mechanical equivalent of English two books with a plural suffix.
Separate semantic plurality from whether Turkish requires the plural morpheme in that construction.

rules.summary_en: Plural marking can also interact with definiteness, collectivity, and agreement choices in the wider sentence.
tips_en: Start with the core noun-phrase rule, then learn discourse-sensitive exceptions separately.
Do not make plural suffix presence your only clue to plural meaning.

rules.summary_en: Polish nouns distinguish singular and plural, with forms determined by gender/class and case.
tips_en: Learn noun number inside the declension system.
Plural endings are not one universal suffix.

rules.summary_en: Numerals trigger important noun-form and agreement patterns, including a major contrast between forms used with many two-to-four combinations and those used with five and above.
tips_en: Treat numeral + noun patterns as grammar constructions.
Compound numerals and case can change the surface pattern, so avoid a one-line English rule.

rules.summary_en: Adjectives and verbs participate in number agreement, with additional distinctions inside the plural agreement system.
tips_en: Use the whole phrase and clause to identify number.
Plural agreement can carry distinctions not visible in an English translation.

forms.display: مفرد / جمع; ـها and other plural patterns

rules.summary_en: Persian commonly forms overt plurals with the productive suffix ها, while other plural patterns also occur.
tips_en: Treat ها as the broad productive default, not the only plural form in the language.
Learn frequent lexicalized or register-sensitive alternatives with the noun.

rules.summary_en: The plural suffix ان occurs with particular noun classes and lexical patterns rather than functioning as a universal alternative.
tips_en: Do not freely swap ها and ان on every noun.
Learn ان plurals where they are established.

rules.summary_en: Overt plural marking is not required in every quantity construction when plurality is already established by a numeral or quantifying expression.
tips_en: Separate plural meaning from obligatory plural morphology.
Read numeral/quantifier constructions as whole phrases.

rules.summary_en: Indonesian nouns do not require an obligatory singular/plural inflection in every noun phrase.
tips_en: Let context, numerals, and quantifiers carry number when they already make it clear.
Do not search for a mandatory Indonesian equivalent of English -s.

rules.summary_en: Full reduplication can express plurality or variety/distributive meanings with many nouns, but it is not simply a required plural suffix strategy.
tips_en: Learn the meaning of the reduplicated construction, not only the visual repetition.
Do not reduplicate automatically after every numeral or quantifier.

rules.summary_en: When an explicit numeral or quantifier already supplies quantity, an additional plural-marking strategy is often unnecessary.
tips_en: Treat the noun phrase as one information package.
Semantic plurality can be fully clear with an unchanged noun.

rules.summary_en: Catalan nouns normally distinguish singular and plural, frequently with -s plus ending-specific spelling and morphological changes.
tips_en: Start from the noun's ending and plural class.
Do not assume every noun is formed by mechanically appending one letter.

rules.summary_en: Some nouns are invariable for number and rely on the surrounding noun phrase to show the contrast.
tips_en: Use determiners and adjectives as evidence when the noun itself does not change.
Unchanged surface form is compatible with grammatical plural.

rules.summary_en: Determiners and adjectives normally agree with the noun in number.
tips_en: Change the agreement chain together.
Treat number as a noun-phrase feature, not only a noun suffix.

rules.summary_en: Galician nouns normally distinguish singular and plural, with plural formation determined by the word's ending and associated spelling patterns.
tips_en: Learn the common ending families rather than one universal suffix rule.
Watch accent and spelling changes in ending-specific patterns.

rules.summary_en: Some noun forms can remain unchanged across singular and plural, leaving determiners or context to show number.
tips_en: Read the whole noun phrase.
No visible noun change does not erase grammatical number.

rules.summary_en: Determiners and adjectives normally agree with the noun in number.
tips_en: Track noun-phrase agreement as a unit.
Agreement provides redundant clues that make number easier to recognize in real text.

rules.summary_en: Macedonian nouns normally distinguish singular and plural, using several plural suffix patterns rather than one universal ending.
tips_en: Learn the noun's productive plural pattern with the noun.
Gender and noun shape help organize the common plural classes.

rules.summary_en: Some masculine nouns have special count forms in numeral constructions, so an explicit quantity does not always use the ordinary plural form.
tips_en: Learn numeral + noun patterns as constructions.
Do not force the ordinary dictionary plural after every number.

rules.summary_en: Adjectives and other agreeing elements can reflect noun-phrase number.
tips_en: Use surrounding agreement as evidence.
Number marking is distributed across the phrase, not only the noun ending.
